questions.question: How would your writing differ if addressing a headteacher versus addressing your peers?

points.text: Headteacher: formal register, respectful tone, evidence-based arguments, no contractions. Peers: informal register, relatable tone, personal examples, contractions acceptable.

questions.question: Explain the difference between writing to persuade and writing to inform.

points.text: Persuade aims to convince the reader to agree or take action, using rhetorical devices and emotional appeal. Inform aims to provide facts objectively, with neutral language and clear explanations.

questions.question: A speech about healthy eating - how would tone differ for primary school children versus adults?

points.text: Primary children: simple vocabulary, fun analogies, engaging tone, direct address like "your body needs..." Adults: more sophisticated vocabulary, statistics and evidence, respectful tone, addressing them as decision-makers.

questions.question: Why is it important to avoid contractions in formal writing?

points.text: Contractions (can't, don't) are associated with speech and informal writing. Writing them in full (cannot, do not) creates a more formal, professional tone suitable for letters to officials, articles, and most exam tasks.
